name: Telegram
description: Chat with Kucedr from Telegram through a configured bot. Access is controlled with enabled state, allowlists, targets, and DM policy.

name: Discord
description: Chat with Kucedr from a Discord server or DM, with threads, reply references, allowlists, and DM policy. Replies route back to the originating channel or thread.

name: Slack
description: Coming-soon workspace channel for team conversations, approvals, and assistant replies in the originating thread.

name: WhatsApp
description: Coming-soon mobile messaging channel for quick personal requests and assistant check-ins.

name: Email
description: Coming-soon asynchronous channel for requests, summaries, and follow-up workflows.

name: Remote MCP servers
description: Connect hosted tool servers over HTTP with optional token or key authentication.

name: Local MCP servers
description: Run stdio tool servers as local processes so domain-specific tools can plug into Kucedr.

name: Skills
description: Install or import reusable workflows that bundle instructions, references, templates, schemas, and optional executable behavior.

name: OpenAI-compatible endpoints
description: Point Kucedr at additional compatible providers by configuring the endpoint and API key.

name: Assistant providers
description: Use your own provider account and model for the chat and agent brain.

name: Speech providers
description: Choose provider and model separately for speech-to-text dictation and text-to-speech read-aloud.

name: Image providers
description: Generate images through the text-to-image provider and model you select.

name: Task scheduler
description: Run recurring assistant jobs such as daily summaries, periodic checks, or routine cleanup.

name: Health checks
description: Have Kucedr run periodically against your checklist and report back on setup health.

name: Local workspace
description: Keep produced files, working data, settings, credentials, memory, and conversation history on your machine.
